bug_semantics: ApproveAttach obtains the boards on which the authenticated user has approve_posts permission, but its per-attachment predicate uses assignment instead of comparison: $allowed_boards = array(0) || in_array(...) (later [0] and \in_array). Because || binds more tightly than =, the non-empty array(0)/[0] left operand is truthy, short-circuits the membership test, and assigns boolean true to $allowed_boards; every queried pending attachment therefore passes the authorization gate. A low-privileged authenticated caller can consequently approve, reject, or delete pending attachments outside boards they may moderate.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable predicate predates the repository's accessible Git history. The sole Git root, a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91 (2012-01-24, message '10610'), is a 1,045-file whole-project snapshot and already contains the flawed line at Sources/ManageAttachments.php:1500. Later commits only preserve or move the same mechanism: 51ad4a4b2c1f7e292501f583d6defed62d56b535 renames ManageAttachments.php, 958840edad356bf237fd19790c36797d163cd383 extracts ApproveAttach into Sources/Actions/AttachmentApprove.php, a86ccb86190d867bd144a76a4c8d777e6c74a7b2 modernizes array(0) to [0], and 74e835324fbdbc594b2e67b068e548e541a163da qualifies in_array. None is the causal introducer. The pre-root SVN revision that first wrote the mistaken '=' cannot be reconstructed from the validated clone, and the legacy svn.simplemachines.org host no longer resolves.
ai_marker: unavailable: the smallest real BIC is before the accessible Git root, so there is no BIC commit object whose author, committer, or trailers can be inspected. The root snapshot a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91 has author and committer 'Spuds <spudsrv@gmail.com>', message '10610', and no trailers, but it is an aggregate import rather than the BIC and is not used for AI attribution.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-62g6-4j9c-6v7p describes the authorization bypass in Sources/Actions/AttachmentApprove.php, affected SMF 2.1 before 2.1.8 and 3.0 before Alpha 5, and references PRs #9181/#9182 plus merge commits a7875e876a647572dd4c45da881b875092caac3d and 7d048f8d66aab9af51cd6ee110fbad103cf673e8. Fix: git show 8a4336e40c8febb8dd6d10b6d833085914bc18ed changes only the 3.0 predicate from '=' to '===' at Sources/Actions/AttachmentApprove.php:103; a7875e876a647572dd4c45da881b875092caac3d is the corresponding PR #9181 merge. Parallel 2.1 direct commit 1a9767b9cb62577efea7f0a62d3e4521e67addd6 makes the same one-character correction in Sources/ManageAttachments.php and is merged by 7d048f8d66aab9af51cd6ee110fbad103cf673e8 (PR #9182). git grep confirms the flawed predicate in v2.1.7 at Sources/ManageAttachments.php:1799 and v3.0-alpha.4 at Sources/Actions/AttachmentApprove.php:103, while the two merge trees contain '==='. git tag --contains a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91 lists every published 2.1 tag through v2.1.7 and every 3.0 tag through v3.0-alpha.4; git branch -r --contains shows the direct corrections on origin/release-2.1 and origin/release-3.0, and git tag --contains on each direct fix is empty because the named patched releases were not tagged in this clone snapshot. Origin trace: repository-wide git log -S and git blame converge on ^a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91; git grep locates the already-flawed predicate in that root at Sources/ManageAttachments.php:1500. git rev-list --max-parents=0 --all returns only a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91, git cat-file -p shows it has no parent, and git diff-tree counts 1,045 added files, proving it is a history-root snapshot rather than a smallest change. Direct fetch of http://svn.simplemachines.org/smf/ fails with DNS ENOTFOUND, so the pre-Git parent tree and originating SVN change are inaccessible.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the assignment operator in the authorization predicate, not the later file moves, class extraction, array-syntax modernization, namespace qualification, or the release merges. The line is demonstrably vulnerable in the last available affected tags and is corrected by the one-line direct commits on both maintained branches. Following the line backward through those semantic-preserving transformations reaches the sole Git root, where it already exists. That root imports 1,045 files and has no parent; treating it as a BIC would violate the protocol's requirement for the smallest commit that first wrote the flaw and would make immediate-parent absence impossible to verify. Since the retired external SVN history is the missing causal predecessor, this is a genuine public-history boundary rather than merely weak reachable evidence. No BIC commit object is available, so an AI/non-AI attribution cannot be made; fix-only and later commit metadata are irrelevant under the BIC-only rule.
remaining_gap: The inaccessible fact is the exact pre-2012 SVN revision that first changed or wrote the ApproveAttach board-permission predicate with '=' instead of comparison, together with that revision's immediate parent tree and commit-object authorship/trailers. The validated full Git clone starts at an aggregate root snapshot that already contains the flaw, and the legacy svn.simplemachines.org repository is unavailable.
